body.text: Overview and Empirical Foundations of Sustainable packaging
Daily focus and environment quietly determine long-term output, making Sustainable packaging worth examining closely. Practical, evidence-backed habits consistently beat short-lived trends.

Sustainable packaging refers to the design, manufacture and use of packaging with the aim of reducing environmental impacts over its life cycle while maintaining its functional and economic requirements. This involves increased use of life cycle inventory (LCI) and life cycle assessment (LCA) to help guide the use of packaging which reduces the environmental impact and ecological footprint. It includes a look at the whole of the supply chain: from basic function, to marketing, and then through to end of life (LCA) and rebirth. Additionally, an eco-cost to value ratio can be useful The goals are to improve the long term viability and quality of life for humans and the longevity of natural ecosystems. Sustainable packaging must meet the functional and economic needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. Sustainability is not necessarily an end state but is a continuing process of improvement. Life-cycle assessment can also be used to compare packaging systems and identify trade-offs between different materials, manufacturing processes and end-of-life scenarios.
